Criterion: Verify that the design of the landing gear system prevents the occurrence of unsafe dynamics, vibrations, or pitching motions for all operational phases of the air vehicle on the ground and during the transition to and from flight. Standard: The air vehicle maintains an acceptable level of dynamic stability for all mission operations on the ground and during the transition to and from flight. There are no adverse dynamics occurring at any time, such as shimmy, gear walk, porpoising or yaw skids. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses and tests. Dynamic and stability analyses verify landing gear damping and stability for all ground operations, and are validated using component characterization, air vehicle ground vibration tests, and taxi tests. Flight testing verifies that all transitional operations to and from flight have no adverse vibration or instability. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.1.2, A.4.4.1.1.2 Pitch Stability; A.3.4.1.1.7, A.4.4.1.1.7 Gear Stability; A.3.4.1.4.5.1, A.4.4.1.4.5.1 Steering characteristics AFGS-87139: 3.2.1.2.b Arrangement; 3.2.1.4 Damping. 14 CFR 23.721-23.745, 25.721-25.738
